names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 9 octombrie.
Read out of saint.gr's line for 9 Οκτωβρίου, «Όσιοι Ανδρόνικος και Αθανασία η συμβία του», with the rank word left off.
The bare name out of days.pravoslavie.ru's name page 193, headed «Андроник Антиохийский, Египетский, прп.», with the rank word and the two epithets left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 9. октобар ст. ст., „Преп. Андроник и супруга му Атанасија.“ — Преп. is the venerable grade this corpus puts in `types` and comes off, so the bare personal name, the first of the heading’s two, is the whole of the form; the heading gives him no epithet. It is the same string this folder already stores as its `ru` form, the two calendars spelling the name identically, and `andronicus-the-apostle` holds it too — a fold read in the `serbian` row’s note and in `scripts/corpus-gate.mjs`.

source.text: days.pravoslavie.ru, 9 октября ст. ст. — «Прпп. Андроника и супруги его Афанасии (V).»
source.note: The rank is the alt text of the second of the day's two icons, «Cовершается служба, не отмеченная в Типиконе никаким знаком» — a service marked in the Typikon with no sign, which is the plain service — and it stands immediately before this line, which names the two of them together. The day's other icon, a polyeleos, stands at the head of the paragraph before the apostle James and is his.

attestations.note: The Russian puts the pair in the fifth century, «(V)», where saint.gr dates them to the year 540, which is the sixth; the folder's `floruit` is left as the Greek page set it and the disagreement is recorded here. Its life adds what the Greek does not: the trade, the thirds he divided his earnings into, the Scetis and the Tabennisiote convent, and the twelve years.

source.text: doxologia.ro, calendarul pe 9 octombrie — «Sfântul Cuvios Andronic»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 9ης Οκτωβρίου — «Όσιοι Ανδρόνικος και Αθανασία η συμβία του»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 9 Οκτωβρίου εκάστου έτους», and the entry is the same couple: the well-off husband and wife of Antioch in Syria, he a money-changer, who lost their two children, went on pilgrimage to the Holy Land and then to Egypt, and by common decision became monastics — he in the monastery of the abba Daniel, she in the women's monastery of the Tabennesiotes — and fell asleep in peace. The page states «έζησαν κατά το έτος 540 μ.Χ.», so a `dates` object is proposed from its own words. It records a portion of the relics of each of them at the monastery of Kykkos in Cyprus. The page prints a proper apolytikion that names them both, taken here, and an «Έτερον Ἀπολυτίκιον», the common «Τῆς ἐρήμου πολίτης», which names Andronicus alone and is taken for his folder only. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence on the life page.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 22.10.2026 (9. октобар ст. ст.) — „Преп. Андроник и супруга му Атанасија.“

attestations.note: The day’s second entry, the first of its two names. The heading is quoted whole, **with the closing full stop the Prologue itself prints**, which is what BRIEF-SERBIAN §4 asks for. It had to be measured off the raw cached page, because `srbody.mjs` and `sr-cand.mjs` both strip it from their printed output: every heading of this day ends `. ` in the source. **An earlier wave of this reading quoted off the stripped output and wrote into its notes that the headings carry no closing stop, which the raw page contradicts for its own days as well as for these** — the rows of that wave are outside this reader’s range and are a finding for the author, not something fixed here. THE HEADING IS AN ENUMERATED COMPANY OF TWO — Андроник and the wife it names, Атанасија — so §5 counts two names, two folders are owed a row, and the corpus holds both. The quoted line is the one heading, whole, on both rows. `dates` UNTOUCHED ON BOTH, AND THE BOOKS ARE IRRECONCILABLE. The two folders hold `floruit` 540 off saint.gr’s «έζησαν κατά το ἔτος 540 μ.Χ.», while the Russian calendar puts the pair in the fifth century and the folders already record that neither is settled. **This entry opens by dating them to the reign of the emperor Theodosius the Great, which is earlier than both** — and it is the Romanian life’s dating, which this folder’s own first sentence already carries. **An emperor is not a source for a year, a reign is not a date, and three books now disagree three ways**, so the field is not touched at all and the disagreement is recorded here. That is the standing instruction where the books cannot be reconciled. `types` UNTOUCHED at `venerable` on both, corroborated by Преп. No `locations`, no `office`. THE ELDER DANIEL AND THE MARTYR JULIAN TAKE NO ROWS, AND BOTH REFUSALS HAVE A NAMED GROUND. The entry sends Andronicus «код старца Данила у Скиту»; the corpus keeps thirteen folders displayed as a Daniel and **not one of them is of Scetis** — the nearest by name, `daniel-the-egyptian`, is a martyr of one of the Palestinian companies under Diocletian and is a different man — so an identification off a bare forename is refused, as the existing lives already refuse it. And the martyr Јулијан **appears** to Athanasia at the graveyard: an appearance is not a relation. The children, the parents and the emperor’s subjects take no rows. WHAT THE BOOK ADDS, AND ONE ITEM IS A NUMBER NO OTHER BOOK GIVES. **Athanasia died first and Andronicus eight days after her** — «најпре св. Атанасија, а после 8 дана и св. Андроник» — where the Romanian life says he died soon afterwards and the Russian soon after her. The martyr Julian’s consolation is also given its **content** for the first time: that their children are in the kingdom of God and are better off there than they would be with their parents on earth, where the Romanian has him merely reprove her sorrow. And the entry says the two children died «у један дан», in one day. WHAT THE BOOK DOES NOT HAVE, SAID BECAUSE SILENCE IS NOT A CORRECTION: this account knows nothing of the second pilgrimage, of the monk who called himself Athanasius, of the twelve years in one cell, or of the letter under the pillow — the whole recognition story of the Romanian and Russian lives is absent, and it stops at long years of ascetic labour. The thirds of the earnings are here as they are elsewhere, though the order differs: a third to the poor, a third to the church, a third to live on. THE FOLD, AND THE SLUG SET DID NOT MOVE. `foldchk.py` measured «Андроник» before this day as `[('andronicus-of-antioch', 'ru'), ('andronicus-the-apostle', 'sr')]` — this folder already held the identical string as its `ru` form, so the new `sr` form adds no folder to the fold and the gate’s key is unchanged. **The gate has been printing that two-folder row as unread all the same**, so the key is written now: `andronicus-the-apostle` is Andronicus of the Seventy, companion of Junia, an apostle, bishop and martyr kept on 17 May, and this folder is the Antiochene goldsmith of 9 October who ended his life a monk in Egypt. Two days, two men, one bare forename. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day carries only the verse.

hymns.text: Locuitor pustiului, înger în trup şi de minuni făcător te-ai arătat, purtătorule de Dumnezeu, Părintele nostru Andronic. Cu postul, cu privegherea şi prin rugăciune primind daruri cereşti, tămăduieşti pe cei bolnavi şi sufletele celor ce aleargă la tine cu credinţă. Slavă Celui Ce ţi-a dat ţie putere; Slavă Celui Ce te-a încununat pe tine; Slavă Celui Ce lucrează prin tine tuturor tămăduiri.

english.text: A dweller of the desert, an angel in the body and a wonderworker thou wast shown to be, our God-bearing father Andronicus. By fasting, by vigil and by prayer thou didst receive heavenly gifts, and thou healest the sick and the souls of them that run to thee in faith. Glory to him who gave thee strength; glory to him who crowned thee; glory to him who through thee worketh healings for all.

hymns.text: Σωφροσύνης τὴν χλαῖναν τὴν θεούφαντον, κατεποικίλατε χρόαις τῶν ἱερῶν ἀρετῶν, ὁμοφρόνως ἐν σπουδῇ ἄμφω ἀσκήσαντες, ὅθεν ὑμῶν τὴν σιωπήν, ἡ τρισάγιος ᾠδή, ἐδέξατο ἐν ὑψίστοις, Ἀνδρόνικε σὺν τὴ θεία, Ἀθανασία τὴ Θεόφρονι.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος πλ. α’, Τὸν συνάναρχον Λόγον — the first hymn on the page of «Όσιοι Ανδρόνικος και Αθανασία η συμβία του», and it names them both.

english.text: You embroidered the God-woven mantle of chastity with the colours of the sacred virtues, both of you living in asceticism with one mind and with zeal; and so the thrice-holy song received your silence in the highest, Andronicus, with the divine and God-minded Athanasia.

hymns.text: Τῆς ἐρήμου πολίτης, καὶ ἐν σώματι ἄγγελος, καὶ θαυματουργὸς ἀνεδείχθης, θεοφόρε πατὴρ ἡμῶν Ἀνδρόνικε, νηστείᾳ, ἀγρυπνίᾳ, προσευχῇ, οὐράνια χαρίσματα λαβών, θεραπεύεις τοὺς νοσοῦντας, καὶ τὰς ψυχάς των πίστει προστρεχόντων σοι· Δόξα τῷ δεδωκότι σοι ἰσχύν, δόξα τῷ σὲ στεφανώσαντι, δόξα τῷ ἐνεργοῦντι διὰ σοῦ πᾶσιν ἰάματα.

source.text: saint.gr, Έτερον Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος α’, Τοῦ λίθου σφραγισθέντος — the second hymn on the page of «Όσιοι Ανδρόνικος και Αθανασία η συμβία του». It is the common of a venerable father, printed with his name in it, «θεοφόρε πατὴρ ἡμῶν Ἀνδρόνικε», and names no other saint; it is taken for his folder alone.

english.text: You were shown to be a citizen of the desert, an angel in the body and a wonderworker, our God-bearing father Andronicus; by fasting, vigil and prayer you received heavenly gifts, and you heal the sick and the souls of those who run to you in faith. Glory to him who gave you strength, glory to him who crowned you, glory to him who works healings for all through you.
